summary: A correction to RFC 107. At the end of its flow control section, the range for a fraction should read zero to 127 rather than zero to 128. The allocation is returned only when the leftmost bit is 1. It was replaced by RFC 154.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 132 corrects one range in RFC 107's flow-control section. The upper bound should be 127, not 128, and the allocation is returned only when the leftmost bit is 1.

questions: what is the error in rfc 107 flow control
what is the correct range in rfc 107 flow control
subtitle: Corrects a range at the end of RFC 107's flow-control section.

tldr.problem: RFC 107's flow-control text gives an upper end of 128 for a range that should end at 127.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 132 says the sentence should specify a range from zero to 127 and clarifies that the allocation is returned only when the high-order bit of the fraction is 1.
tldr.outcome: This correction to RFC 107 was itself obsoleted by RFC 154.

today: RFC 132 is historic and was obsoleted by RFC 154. It records a correction to the flow-control text in RFC 107.

sections.title: The Typographical Correction
sections.content: RFC 132 points to a sentence on page 5 of RFC 107, in the section titled “V. Flow Control.” The sentence says that a number is in range zero to 128. RFC 132 says the range should instead be zero to 127.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 107 gives the wrong upper bound for a range. This one-page note corrects it from 128 to 127.

sections.title: When the Allocation Is Returned
sections.content: The correction states that the appropriate allocation is returned only if the high-order, or leftmost, bit of the corresponding fraction is 1. This clarifies the condition attached to the corrected range in the original flow-control text.
sections.plainLanguage: The note also states the condition for returning the allocation: the fraction's leftmost bit must be 1.

sections.title: Status of the Correction
sections.content: RFC 132 is a short correction to RFC 107. The unit metadata records RFC 154 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 132.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo fixed a line in RFC 107. RFC 154 later replaced RFC 132.
